label: Digitally Immersed & Emotionally Distressed
summary: This profile represents highly educated women who spend more than 5 hours daily online and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. With a UCLA-8 loneliness mean of 1.74, a PHQ-9 depression mean of 1.75, and a notably high GAD-7 anxiety mean of 2.17, this group consistently scores above moderate thresholds across all three psychological distress dimensions. Their extensive screen time may both reflect and reinforce social isolation and emotional difficulties.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, daily screen/internet use exceeding 5 hours
behavior_markers: Extended daily screen time (more than 5 hours)
Elevated self-reported loneliness despite high educational attainment
Highest anxiety levels among profiles, suggesting persistent worry or tension
Potential reliance on digital environments as a substitute for in-person social connection
tone: Concerned and empathetic, reflecting the co-occurrence of multiple psychological distress indicators in a high-functioning demographic group

label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
summary: This profile represents respondents who report notably low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. They demonstrate strong psychological well-being across all three measured dimensions, with anxiety scores near floor level and depression and loneliness scores well below typical thresholds of concern.
demographic_anchor: Male, graduate-level education or above, 1–3 hours of daily screen/internet use
behavior_markers: Reports minimal loneliness (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 0.77, well below clinical concern)
Exhibits very low depressive symptomatology (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.33)
Moderate and controlled screen/internet usage (1–3 hours daily)
Higher educational attainment suggesting structured daily routines and social engagement
tone: Stable, emotionally resilient, and psychologically well-adjusted

label: Lonely but Emotionally Resilient
summary: This profile captures respondents who report notably elevated loneliness yet maintain relatively low levels of depressive and anxiety symptoms. Despite feeling socially disconnected, they do not exhibit the emotional distress patterns typically associated with loneliness, suggesting a degree of psychological resilience or effective coping mechanisms that buffer against mood and anxiety disorders.
demographic_anchor: Predominantly female, holding graduate-level or higher education, reporting 1–3 hours of daily screen time or social media use
behavior_markers: Elevated loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 1.30) indicating moderate-to-high perceived social isolation
Low depressive symptom burden (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.86) well below clinical thresholds
Low anxiety symptom levels (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.91) suggesting minimal worry or nervousness
Moderate and controlled digital engagement (1–3 hours daily)
Possible reliance on academic or professional pursuits as a coping outlet given high educational attainment
tone: Quietly disconnected yet emotionally stable; introspective rather than distressed
